scope: Evidence for one physical AC1024 LayerStates XRECORD and its source-bounded dictionary/control/dependency graph. A narrowly selected producer-compatibility route emits its group-370 Int16 field. The selected source-projected graph now passes production ASCII and Binary DXF output plus fresh libdxfrw readback, including its nested SCALE dependency and the complete ACAD_SCALELIST closure. This does not qualify native LayerStates semantics or whole-source conversion.

independent_producer_evidence.observed: LibreDWG emits XRECORD 0x249, owner 0x1B8, with group 370 value -3.
independent_producer_evidence.scope_limit: This corroborates a producer output profile only. It does not establish Autodesk-standard XRECORD semantics or native LayerStates restoration. A subsequent LibreDWG JSON reread attempt returned ERROR 0x800 and is not claimed as reader acceptance.

autodesk_xrecord.title: Autodesk AutoCAD DXF Reference, XRECORD (DXF)
autodesk_xrecord.rule: XRECORD application values use group codes 1-369 except 5 and 105; group 370 is outside this documented application domain.

autodesk_xrecord_group_table.title: Autodesk ObjectARX Developer Guide, DXF Group Codes for Xrecords
autodesk_xrecord_group_table.rule: The XRECORD-specific table ends at 360-369 and does not define group 370 application data.

autodesk_general_group_table.title: Autodesk DXF Group Codes in Numerical Order Reference
autodesk_general_group_table.rule: Groups 370-379 are signed 16-bit lineweight enum values; custom non-entity objects may use the full range. This general table does not override the narrower XRECORD-specific rule.

rules: The dedicated group-370 predicate is separate from the standard XRECORD application-code predicate and from the existing DWG 1070/1071 compatibility route.
The adapter admits this field only for the source-bound selected LayerStates XRECORD from an AC1024 DWG, with target AC1024, unchanged captured source identity, INTEGER type, and signed Int16 range.
Ordinary XRECORD writing remains fail-closed for group 370. The explicit compatibility writer is not a general XRECORD API path; the adapter invokes it only for the selected source-qualified record.
DWG parsing sign-normalizes group 370 from raw 16-bit storage so source 0xFFFD is represented as -3, matching the independent LibreDWG producer output.

focused_case.result: PASS. Confirms the physical AC1024 source identity and group-370 producer profile; ordinary ASCII/Binary XRECORD writes refuse group 370 and preserve destination and caller fields; compatibility output rejects an AC1021 target and an out-of-Int16 value; corrected retry and fresh readback preserve exact fields, ordering and handle references. Production fileExport then emits the selected source-projected LayerStates graph in ASCII and Binary, and fresh fileImport confirms the LAYER_CONTROL edge, three LayerStates roots, companion dictionaries, XRECORD extension dictionary, nested XRECORD, exact LAYER/LTYPE references, unique ACAD_SCALELIST root/owner, and all 32 SCALE records and fields. A nested SCALE reference mutation to 0xDEADBEEF is rejected with an existing destination sentinel and caller-owned mutation preserved; restoring the reference and retrying through the same writer succeeds.
focused_case.coverage_limit: The production graph check uses a test-only projection of this physical DWG source. It retains the selected LayerStates graph, required LAYER/LTYPE tables and the complete ACAD_SCALELIST dependency while excluding unrelated named-object roots, including the known invalid SUN owner outlier. This is not whole-source conversion or native LayerStates restoration/evaluation evidence.

limitations: The physical DWG is an existing local investigation input and was not added to the repository.
The producer-specific group-370 exception does not widen the generic XRECORD domain and cannot be generalized to other sources or codes.
The production LayerStates graph result is a test-only source projection; unrelated named-object roots, including the invalid SUN owner outlier, remain excluded and fail-closed.
Fresh libdxfrw readback does not establish native LayerStates restoration/evaluation semantics or promote a support claim.
No whole-source conversion or independent native LayerStates acceptance is claimed.
